title: One-step CRISPR-Cas9-mediated knockout of native TCRαβ genes in human T cells
author: Flumens, Campillo-Davo, et al.

steps.title: Isolate PBMC from buffy coats
steps.instruction: Perform density‑gradient centrifugation to obtain peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) from donor buffy coats.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PBS/EDTA buffer and pre‑heat to 37 °C.
Wipe the blood tube of the buffy‑coat bag with 70 % ethanol and cut the tube to release the blood (maintain sterility).
Divide the buffy coat into sterile 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes (~10 mL blood per tube).
Dilute each tube 1:3 with pre‑heated PBS/EDTA (e.g., add 20 mL buffer to 10 mL blood to reach 30 mL total). Add the buffer quickly for thorough mixing. (If starting from whole blood, dilute 1:2.)
Carefully layer 12 mL Ficoll‑Paque PLUS underneath the diluted blood without mixing.
Centrifuge at 740 × g for 30 min at 19–22 °C in a swinging‑bucket rotor; use low acceleration and turn off the rotor brake.
Collect the PBMC layer:
• Remove ~2/3 of the upper plasma layer, leaving a small plasma volume on the interphase.
• Loosen PBMC adhering to the tube wall with the tip of a 10 mL pipette.
• Aspirate the PBMC interphase and transfer to a clean sterile 50 mL Falcon tube; discard the remaining Ficoll and RBC layers.
Repeat the collection for each centrifuge tube.
Add PBS/EDTA to bring the volume to 40 mL and centrifuge at 480 × g for 5 min at 19–22 °C (maximal acceleration, brake on).
Discard the supernatant and resuspend each pellet in 10 mL PBS/EDTA; pool the suspensions into two 50 mL tubes.
Repeat the washing step (add PBS/EDTA to 40 mL, centrifuge 480 × g, 5 min, 19–22 °C).
Discard supernatant and pool all cells into one 50 mL tube, resuspending in a final volume of 50 mL PBS/EDTA.
Count cells with an automatic cell counter; transfer 100 000 PBMC to a polystyrene FACS tube for viability testing.
Add 100 µL FACS buffer, stain with 0.5 µL propidium iodide (1 mg/mL), incubate 1 min at 19–22 °C, then measure viability on a flow cytometer (expected 95 %–99 %).

steps.title: Assess PBMC viability and store
steps.instruction: After viability assessment, keep or cryopreserve the isolated PBMC for later use.

substeps.instruction: If using immediately, keep PBMC on a roller shaker for up to 16 h in serum‑free AIM‑V medium at 1–1.6 × 10⁷ cells/mL.
For cryopreservation, resuspend cells at 0.5–1 × 10⁸ cells/mL in 90 % FBS + 10 % DMSO, then store at –80 °C for short‑term or below –150 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Analyze transfection efficiency by flow
steps.instruction: Determine the percentage of EGFP‑positive T cells 24 h after electroporation using flow cytometry.

substeps.instruction: Take 100 000 electroporated CD8⁺ T cells and transfer to a polystyrene FACS tube.
Add 2 mL FACS buffer and centrifuge at 480 × g for 5 min at 19–22 °C.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 100 µL FACS buffer.
Acquire the sample on a flow cytometer and calculate the proportion of EGFP⁺ cells (expected 80 %–90 %).
